newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: China containment a dangerous policy - Australia.
newsitem.headline: China containment a dangerous policy - Australia.

text.p: Australia's chief diplomat warned on Friday that any attempt to contain China's increasing economic and strategic clout would be dangerous.
"Those that see in China's economic growth a threat which needs to be contained advocate a dangerously wrong-headed policy," foreign affairs department secretary Phillip Flood said in a speech.

"Our interests -- and indeed the interests of China -- are best served by its active and positive involvement in regional and international affairs," Flood told the Australian Institute of International Affairs.

Beijing fears the United States is pursuing a policy of containment towards China by bolstering defence ties with countries like Japan and Australia and campaigning on Chinese human rights issues such as Tibet.
Containment was a U.S. Cold War strategy to prevent the spread of communism from the Soviet bloc.
Washington denies it has a policy of containment of China, saying economic and political engagement with Beijing is the best way to push for protection of human rights.
Australia also rejects containment although its own relations with China were strained over a recent visit by Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama.

"The advantages for China and other countries of the region will be maximised by working co-operatively together with China in this period of its strong economic growth and increasing confidence in its own position," Flood said.
This was particularly true of China's bilateral relationships with Japan and the United States, he added.
